source_name: Budapest Fintech Week (HFA + Startup Hungary) – partner/sponsor roster
source_subtype: event landing page with partner list
why_relevant: Community-organised Hungarian fintech week (2025 edition 4–5 Dec, KPMG Conference Center Budapest) whose named collaborators are themselves a partnership disclosure: Hungarian Fintech Association, Startup Hungary, Ergomania, HOLD Fund Management, KPMG Hungary, Visa and CIB Bank. Shows which bank and card-scheme money backs the local fintech community.

source_name: Fintech.hu – Hungarian fintech portal, event tag feeds
why_relevant: HU-language fintech portal that promotes regional events (e.g. Money Motion in Zagreb, flagged as the region's largest fintech event with prominent Hungarian participation) and carries event tag archives. Useful for catching Hungarian vendors and banks that exhibit at CEE-regional events rather than domestic ones.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) – press releases and annual conference
why_relevant: The banking association holds anniversary/annual conferences (35th jubilee conference with bank CEOs, government leaders and 11 foreign banking-association delegates) and runs recurring programmes such as PÉNZ7 (2–6 March 2026, 12th edition) whose partner and supporter lists include banks and technology suppliers. Its working-group (munkacsoportok) page identifies which topics have institutional vendor engagement.

source_name: HUNGEXPO / Sirha Budapest – exhibitor directory (kiállítói lista)
why_relevant: Hungary's main trade-fair operator publishes a structured, searchable exhibitor list per fair. Sirha Budapest (HORECA/food) is the fair where POS terminals, cash registers (pénztárgép) and merchant payment acceptance vendors exhibit to the merchant side rather than the bank side — i.e. the acquiring/merchant-services channel that banking conferences miss. Same directory pattern applies to other HUNGEXPO fairs.

source_name: Az Év Honlapja (Website of the Year) – winners archive
why_relevant: Hungary's main digital/web award with a per-year winners archive that regularly includes finance-category entries; entries are usually submitted by the agency or implementation partner alongside the bank, so the winners list doubles as a bank↔digital-supplier partnership register. Purely professional recognition (no cash prize), so entries reflect real vendor marketing intent.

source_name: paytech.events – Fintech, Banking & Payments conference calendar 2026–2027
why_relevant: Aggregated international calendar of payments/banking events; useful to discover Hungary-hosted or Hungary-relevant CEE events not indexed by HU-language sources, and to catch which regional events Hungarian banks/vendors attend. Aggregator, so cross-verify each entry against the organiser site.

source_name: bankweb.hu – IIR Magyarország Kártyapiac konferencia coverage
why_relevant: Secondary HU banking portal that reproduces card-market conference agendas and speaker lists; a useful fallback when the IIR legacy site's archive pages are unreachable, and an independent record of which vendors and banks presented.

source_name: e-cégjegyzék – Céginformációs és Elektronikus Cégeljárásban Közreműködő Szolgálat (official Hungarian company register portal)
source_subtype: official company register / primary filing portal
why_relevant: Statutory company register of Hungary: legal name, cégjegyzékszám, seat, share capital, owners (tagok/részvényesek), representatives, TEÁOR/NACE codes and status for every Hungarian legal entity, including local subsidiaries of foreign banking/payments vendors. This is the authoritative anchor record for any vendor or competitor entity in the HU market.

source_name: Cégszolgálat Online Céginformáció (occsz.e-cegjegyzek.hu) – paid authenticated certificate query system
why_relevant: The transactional front-end of the official register where hiteles cégkivonat, cégbizonyítvány, cégmásolat and filed company documents (deeds of foundation, ownership changes) can be pulled for ~1.5m current and dissolved entities. Company documents reveal shareholder changes, capital injections and quiet acquisitions of HU vendors by foreign groups.

source_name: Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál (e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu) – annual accounts filing & search
why_relevant: Mandatory annual financial statements (beszámoló: mérleg, eredménykimutatás, kiegészítő melléklet, sometimes üzleti jelentés) for every Hungarian company, free to download as PDF/XBRL-like files. This is the single best evidence base for vendor revenue trends, headcount, export share and — in the kiegészítő melléklet — occasionally named large customers or parent-company relations, i.e. who is actually winning bank work.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat – Beszámoló állomány értékesítése (bulk sale of the full filings dataset)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Justice sells the complete annual-accounts dataset in bulk. For a systematic HU market model this is the legitimate, licensable alternative to scraping — it enables NACE/TEÁOR-based screening of the whole IT-and-payments supplier population rather than a hand-built watchlist.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat (Ministry of Justice) – institutional hub page
why_relevant: Master pointer to every official HU company-data channel: free company information, filing submission (OBR), bulk dataset sales, direct company announcements, and the legal basis for each. Best single page to re-check when portals move or rules change.

source_name: Cégközlöny – official company gazette (cegkozlony.hu)
why_relevant: Court-ordered publication of company formations, data changes, mergers/demergers, liquidation and strike-off. Free full-issue download and search. This is where a quiet market entry (new HU subsidiary of a foreign payments vendor) or an exit first becomes public — often before any press coverage.

source_name: CKK – Cégközlöny közvetlen közlemények rendszere (direct company announcements)
why_relevant: Companies' own statutory notices (transformations, capital reductions, creditor calls, demergers). For vendor tracking these are early signals of restructuring, carve-outs and group reorganisations that precede M&A or market exit.

source_name: OPTEN Cégtár / OPTEN webshop céginfó
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian commercial company-information house. Cégtár holds all Cégközlöny-published register data incl. deleted companies, plus cégtörténet, pénzügyi beszámoló, Kapcsolati Háló / Címkapcsolati Háló (ownership and address link networks) — the most efficient way to map a foreign vendor's HU subsidiary web and interlocking directorships without pulling dozens of individual filings.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár (nemzeticegtar.hu) – free company search (Opten + Corvinus)
why_relevant: Free tier of Opten data covering ~600k HU companies: owners, registered capital, financial-statement figures, plus flags for public-procurement wins and EU grants. Confirmed to carry the exact vendor entities of interest (NCR Magyarország Kft., Diebold Nixdorf Kft., Diebold Hungary Önkiszolgáló Megoldások Kft. 'v.a.'), making it the cheapest first-pass screen for vendor entity discovery.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Hungary (formerly Bisnode D&B Magyarország) – céginformációs lekérdezés
why_relevant: International company-data provider with a Hungarian entity and HU-language product line; the practical route to link a HU subsidiary to its global parent via DUNS and global corporate-family trees — exactly what is needed to see which foreign banking/payments group sits behind a local Kft.

source_name: Céginfo.hu – company profile aggregator
why_relevant: Free/freemium company profile pages combining register data and financial-statement figures; useful as a cross-check and for quick revenue trend reads on vendor entities (confirmed page for Diebold Nixdorf Kft.).

source_name: iCégtár (icegtar.com) – company profiles with revenue, headcount and won tenders
why_relevant: Aggregator that pairs financial data with 'nyertes pályázatok' (won tenders/grants) per company — a cheap way to see which vendors are winning publicly funded work, a proxy for bank/public-sector delivery activity.

source_name: Céginformáció.hu – cégkereső és hiteles cégkivonat szolgáltató
why_relevant: One of the licensed commercial distributors of the official register; alternative access channel for cégkivonat when the state portal is inconvenient, and a searchable index of HU entities.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal – Business registers in EU countries: Hungary (BRIS)
why_relevant: EU-level gateway (BRIS 'Find a company') giving cross-border access to basic HU company data and, crucially, linking HU entities to their parent/branch registrations in other member states — the fastest way to trace a foreign payments vendor's EU corporate structure into Hungary. Also the authoritative English-language description of what the HU register contains and how to access it.

source_name: NAV adatbázisok – taxpayer databases (áfaalanyok, köztartozásmentes adózói adatbázis, multi-query)
why_relevant: Free official verification layer: VAT-registration status, group VAT numbers, enforcement proceedings and debt-free status per adószám. Confirms whether a vendor entity is genuinely trading in HU (vs. dormant shell), and enforcement/tax-debt flags are early distress signals for competitors.

source_name: KSH statisztikai számjel lekérdező (KSH company base-data query)
why_relevant: Official mapping from adószám to statisztikai számjel, main TEÁOR'25 activity, legal form and county of seat. TEÁOR (the HU national version of NACE) is the classification key for building the universe of banking/payments IT suppliers (e.g. 6201, 6202, 6209, 6311, 4651, 6612, 6619).

source_name: Központi tényleges tulajdonosi nyilvántartás (TTNY / UBO register, AFAD Act) – NAV information pages
source_subtype: restricted-access statutory register (documented via public info pages)
why_relevant: Hungary's central beneficial-ownership register, operated under the AFAD Act. Not open to the public — access is restricted to authorities, supervisors and obliged service providers — but it defines the legal UBO layer and shows what ownership data exists behind the cégjegyzék. Important to document as a known, deliberately closed source so ownership questions are routed to cégkivonat/Opten instead.

source_name: Cégtaláló (cegtalalo.hu) – instant authenticated cégkivonat reseller
why_relevant: Commercial reseller of the official e-cégjegyzék extract; a practical fallback channel when the state portal's authentication flow is impractical for a foreign analyst without Hungarian e-ID.

source_name: OPTEN webshop entity pages for payments/banking vendors (worked examples)
why_relevant: Concrete proof that the register/aggregator layer resolves the actual actor set for this sector: Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (Vecsés, ex-Wincor Nixdorf Kft., IT/telecom wholesale, FY2024 net revenue reported ~9.45bn HUF), NCR Magyarország Kft., Diebold Hungary Önkiszolgáló Megoldások Kft. 'v.a.' (in voluntary liquidation — an exit signal), Bisnode Magyarország Kft. / Dun & Bradstreet Hungary Kft. These pages give the cégjegyzékszám needed to pull the authoritative beszámoló.

source_name: Cégjegyzék.hu – index of free and paid Hungarian company-data services
why_relevant: Curated pointer page comparing the Hungarian cégadat-lekérdezés landscape (free vs paid channels). Useful for periodically re-discovering new or renamed aggregators in this cell.

source_name: OBR – Online Beszámoló Űrlapkitöltő Rendszer (filing submission system) and its FAQ
why_relevant: Documents the filing mechanics, deadlines and file formats behind the annual accounts. Understanding OBR file structure and the publication calendar is what makes a reliable annual collection routine possible (and explains gaps, late filings and corrections).
